name: Hangboard Recruitment Pull
summary: An overcoming isometric finger-strength exercise performed by pulling at maximal effort with one arm against an unyielding hangboard edge while standing on the floor.

setup: Stand directly beneath a securely mounted hangboard with your feet firmly planted on the floor or a stable platform.
Grip the target edge with one hand using a half-crimp or open-hand grip.
Position your working arm overhead with a slight bend in the elbow, maintaining an elbow angle between 120 and 150 degrees rather than full lockout.
steps: Engage your shoulder blade down and back to set your shoulder girdle firmly.
Gradually ramp up tension through your fingers, arm, and back over one to two seconds until reaching maximal pulling effort.
Pull downward against the edge as hard as possible while keeping your feet anchored to the floor.
Maintain maximal effort for three to five seconds without letting your grip position deform.
Smoothly decrease tension and release the hold.
instructions.breathing: Inhale before ramping up tension, then exhale forcefully through pursed lips while sustaining the maximal isometric pull.

common_faults.fault: Jerking into the pull abruptly rather than smoothly ramping tension.
common_faults.correction: Take one to two seconds to build up from submaximal to maximal force to protect finger pulleys and connective tissue.
Maintain a gentle 120 to 150 degree bend at the elbow to properly engage the upper arm and shoulder musculature.

common_faults.fault: Letting the shoulder shrug upward into the ear during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Depress and retract the scapula before initiating force, keeping the shoulder active throughout.

precautions: Ensure fingers and upper body are thoroughly warmed up before attempting maximal isometric efforts.
Do not use a full closed crimp with thumb wrapped to minimize stress on the A2 pulley.
